data.narrative:
Emerald AI, founded by Varun Sivaram, is a Seed-stage climate and energy company that has raised $68M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a broader frontier-tech comp universe spanning climate and energy, encompassing 1 public comparable (LNZA) and 8 private peers including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

A single applicable valuation method was employed: Stage-Progression analysis. This approach applies a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to next-stage funding, grounded in the $68M total raised as a proxy for current value. This yields an implied valuation of $170M. Peer-Median analysis was not applicable; while 8 same-sector comparables exist, none satisfied the narrow filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier peers. A wider all-sector median would introduce undue noise and was rejected.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $144M (low) to $195M (high), with a median of $170M. Material uncertainty remains given the single-method reliance; broader peer comparability constraints in frontier climate tech mean this range should be treated as preliminary. Sensitivity to the 2.5x step-up multiplier assumption and the use of total raised as a value proxy represent key valuation risks. Further refinement would benefit from clearer stage-transition data within the climate tech subset or revenue-based benchmarking as the company matures.
